claim: Human lung adenocarcinoma exhibits a propensity for de-differentiation.
source: Human lung adenocarcinoma exhibits a propensity for de-differentiation, complicating diagnosis and treatment, and predicting poorer patient survival.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general characteristic of human lung adenocarcinoma.

claim: De-differentiation of human lung adenocarcinoma complicates diagnosis and treatment.
source: Human lung adenocarcinoma exhibits a propensity for de-differentiation, complicating diagnosis and treatment, and predicting poorer patient survival.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a consequence of de-differentiation.

claim: De-differentiation of human lung adenocarcinoma predicts poorer patient survival.
source: Human lung adenocarcinoma exhibits a propensity for de-differentiation, complicating diagnosis and treatment, and predicting poorer patient survival.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a prognostic consequence of de-differentiation.

claim: Expression of the BRAFV600E oncoprotein kinase initiates the growth of benign tumors retaining characteristics of their cell of origin, AT2 pneumocytes, in genetically engineered mouse models of lung cancer.
source: In genetically engineered mouse models of lung cancer, expression of the BRAFV600E oncoprotein kinase initiates the growth of benign tumors retaining characteristics of their cell of origin, AT2 pneumocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is based on experimental observations in mouse models.

claim: Cooperating alterations that activate PI3'-lipid signaling promote progression of BRAFV600E-driven benign tumors to malignant adenocarcinoma.
source: Cooperating alterations that activate PI3'-lipid signaling promote progression of BRAFV600E-driven benign tumors to malignant adenocarcinoma.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is based on experimental observations in mouse models.

claim: BrafCAT mice carry a conditional BrafCAT allele in which CRE-mediated recombination leads to co-expression of BRAFV600E and tdTomato.
source: To address this, we generated mice carrying a conditional BrafCAT allele in which CRE-mediated recombination leads to co-expression of BRAFV600E and tdTomato.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the newly generated mouse model.

claim: Co-expression of BRAFV600E and PIK3CAH1047R in AT2 pneumocytes leads to rapid cell de-differentiation.
source: We demonstrate that co-expression of BRAFV600E and PIK3CAH1047R in AT2 pneumocytes leads to rapid cell de-differentiation, without decreased expression of the transcription factors NKX2-1, FOXA1, or FOXA2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is based on experimental observations in the BrafCAT mouse model.

claim: Co-expression of BRAFV600E and PIK3CAH1047R in AT2 pneumocytes leads to rapid cell de-differentiation without decreased expression of the transcription factors NKX2-1, FOXA1, or FOXA2.
source: We demonstrate that co-expression of BRAFV600E and PIK3CAH1047R in AT2 pneumocytes leads to rapid cell de-differentiation, without decreased expression of the transcription factors NKX2-1, FOXA1, or FOXA2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is based on experimental observations in the BrafCAT mouse model.

claim: PGC1α plays a novel role in maintaining AT2 pneumocyte identity.
source: Instead, we propose a novel role for PGC1α in maintaining AT2 pneumocyte identity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a proposed mechanism based on the study's findings.

claim: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the leading cause of cancer-related death.
source: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the leading cause of cancer-related death, with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) being the most common NSCLC subtype (Siegel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common NSCLC subtype.
source: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the leading cause of cancer-related death, with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) being the most common NSCLC subtype (Siegel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: ~75% of LUADs display mutational activation of key components of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling that promote activation of RAS and its key downstream effectors: the RAF→MEK→ERK→MAP kinase (MAPK) and the PI3'-lipid pathways.
source: To that end, since the original discovery of KRAS mutations in human lung cancer cells (Capon et al., 1983), it has emerged that ~75% of LUADs display mutational activation of key components of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling that, in turn, promote activation of RAS and its key downstream effectors: the RAF→MEK→ERK→MAP kinase (MAPK) and the PI3'-lipid pathways (Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2014; Heist and Engelman, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Mutational activation of RTKs or downstream signaling proteins (e.g. EGFR/ERBB1, ALK, ROS1, NTRK, BRAF) serve as predictive biomarkers for the clinical deployment of FDA-approved inhibitors of these oncoprotein kinases for the treatment of genetically-defined subsets of lung cancer.
source: Moreover, mutational activation of RTKs or downstream signaling proteins (e.g. EGFR/ERBB1, ALK, ROS1, NTRK, BRAF) serve as predictive biomarkers for the clinical deployment of FDA-approved inhibitors of these oncoprotein kinases for the treatment of genetically-defined subsets of lung cancer (Drilon et al., 2018; Hyman et al., 2015; Rosell et al., 2012; Scagliotti et al., 2010; Shaw et al., 2013; Shaw et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Mutational activation of BRAF occurs in ~8% of LUAD.
source: Mutational activation of BRAF occurs in ~8% of LUAD, with the most common single mutation (BRAFT1799A) encoding the BRAFV600E oncoprotein kinase (Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: The most common single BRAF mutation (BRAFT1799A) encodes the BRAFV600E oncoprotein kinase.
source: Mutational activation of BRAF occurs in ~8% of LUAD, with the most common single mutation (BRAFT1799A) encoding the BRAFV600E oncoprotein kinase (Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: BrafCA mice carry a CRE-activated allele of Braf that expresses normal BRAF prior to CRE-mediated recombination, after which BRAFV637E (orthologous to human BRAFV600E) is expressed from the endogenous chromosomal locus.
source: To model BRAFV600E driven cancers, we previously described BrafCA mice carrying a CRE-activated allele of Braf that expresses normal BRAF prior to CRE-mediated recombination, after which BRAFV637E (orthologous to human BRAFV600E and for simplicity henceforth referred to as BRAFV600E), is expressed from the endogenous chromosomal locus (Dankort et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: The BrafCA mouse has proven useful in modeling many cancer types in which BRAFV600E is implicated as a driver oncoprotein.
source: This mouse has proven useful in modeling many cancer types in which BRAFV600E is implicated as a driver oncoprotein (Charles et al., 2011; Dankort et al., 2009; Sakamoto et al., 2017; Trejo et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: BRAF mutation serves as a foundational initiating event for tumorigenesis in many target tissues.
source: Taken together, these studies indicate that BRAF mutation serves as a foundational initiating event for tumorigenesis in many target tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on inference from cited studies.

claim: The progression of benign tumors initiated by BRAFV600E expression into malignant cancer invariably requires additional events such as silencing of tumor suppressors (e.g. INK4A-ARF, TP53, PTEN, CDX2) or activation of cooperating oncogenes (PIK3CA, CTNNB1, c-MYC).
source: However, the progression of benign tumors initiated by BRAFV600E expression into malignant cancer invariably requires additional events such as silencing of tumor suppressors (e.g. INK4A-ARF, TP53, PTEN, CDX2) or activation of cooperating oncogenes (PIK3CA, CTNNB1, c-MYC) (Charles et al., 2014; Dankort et al., 2007; Dankort et al., 2009; Huillard et al., 2012; Juan et al., 2014; Sakamoto et al., 2017; Trejo et al., 2013; Tsao et al., 2004; Yu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: There are key similarities between the early stages of tumorigenesis observed in response to expression of either the KRASG12D or BRAFV600E oncoproteins in mouse models of lung carcinogenesis.
source: In mouse models of lung carcinogenesis, there are key similarities between the early stages of tumorigenesis observed in response to expression of either the KRASG12D or BRAFV600E oncoproteins (Dankort et al., 2007; Trejo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Tumors initiated by BRAFV600E remain as benign adenomas with certain features of senescence.
source: While tumors initiated by BRAFV600E remain as benign adenomas with certain features of senescence (Dankort et al., 2007; Jackson et al., 2001), a proportion of KRASG12D initiated lung tumors progress to frank adenocarcinomas within six months, most likely due to the ability of KRASG12D to activate the PI3'-kinase signaling pathway (Castellano et al., 2013; Murillo et al., 2018; Rodriguez-Viciana et al., 1994; Vivanco and Sawyers, 2002; Yuan and Cantley, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: A proportion of KRASG12D initiated lung tumors progress to frank adenocarcinomas within six months, most likely due to the ability of KRASG12D to activate the PI3'-kinase signaling pathway.
source: While tumors initiated by BRAFV600E remain as benign adenomas with certain features of senescence (Dankort et al., 2007; Jackson et al., 2001), a proportion of KRASG12D initiated lung tumors progress to frank adenocarcinomas within six months, most likely due to the ability of KRASG12D to activate the PI3'-kinase signaling pathway (Castellano et al., 2013; Murillo et al., 2018; Rodriguez-Viciana et al., 1994; Vivanco and Sawyers, 2002; Yuan and Cantley, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Co-expression of BRAFV600E and PIK3CAH1047R in AT2 pneumocytes leads to rapid growth of lung tumors, many of which display progression to frank malignancy bearing various hallmarks of the cognate human disease.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, co-expression of BRAFV600E and PIK3CAH1047R, a mutationally-activated form of PI3'-kinase-α (PI3Kα), in AT2 pneumocytes leads to rapid growth of lung tumors, many of which display progression to frank malignancy bearing various hallmarks of the cognate human disease (Kinross et al., 2012; Trejo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Genetically manipulated mice provide a unique opportunity to genetically and biochemically separate and analyze the effects of activation of the RAF→MEK→ERK and PI3'-lipid pathways individually or in combination.
source: Thus, these genetically manipulated mice provide a unique opportunity to genetically and biochemically separate and analyze the effects of activation of these two critical downstream arms of RTK→RAS signaling individually or in combination.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a rationale for the study.

claim: It is not trivial to identify and isolate pure populations of tumor cells without significant stromal contamination in the original BrafCA mouse, particularly in contexts when tumor cells are rare.
source: For example, it is not trivial to identify and isolate pure populations of tumor cells without significant stromal contamination, particularly in contexts when tumor cells are rare, such as in the earliest stages of tumorigenesis, or in the context of minimal residual disease following pathway-targeted inhibition of BRAFV600E signaling (Dankort et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of the original BrafCA mouse.

claim: The mT-mG allele expresses tdTomato before CRE-mediated recombination and EGFP after CRE-mediated recombination.
source: To address these issues we and others have used mice carrying CRE-activated alleles that express fluorescent proteins, such as the mT-mG allele in which the activity of CRE recombinase silences the expression of tdTomato and elicits expression of EGFP (Muzumdar et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Not all cells expressing the desired oncoprotein also express EGFP and vice versa when using the mT-mG allele approach.
source: However, this approach is confounded by the observation that not all cells expressing the desired oncoprotein also express EGFP and vice versa.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of the mT-mG allele approach.

claim: BrafCAT mice carry a new CRE-activated Braf allele that encodes normal BRAF prior to CRE-mediated recombination, after which the recombined allele expresses a bicistronic BrafT1910A-P2A-tdTomato mRNA encoding both BRAFV600E and the red fluorophore tdTomato.
source: In order to unequivocally identify BRAFV600E expressing cells we have generated BrafCAT mice carrying a new CRE-activated Braf allele. Like the original BrafCA allele, BrafCAT encodes normal BRAF prior to CRE-mediated recombination, after which the recombined allele expresses a bicistronic BrafT1910A-P2A-tdTomato mRNA encoding both BRAFV600E and the red fluorophore tdTomato.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a description of the newly generated mouse model.

claim: BRAFV600E-driven lung tumors maintain expression of markers of AT2 identity, including the known regulators of AT2 identity, NKX2-1, FOXA1, and FOXA2.
source: In brief, BRAFV600E-driven lung tumors maintain expression of markers of AT2 identity, including the known regulators of AT2 identity, NKX2-1, FOXA1, and FOXA2 (Bruno et al., 1995; Camolotto et al., 2018; DeFelice et al., 2003; Hamvas et al., 2013; Lazzaro et al., 1991; Minoo et al., 1995; Snyder et al., 2013; Stahlman et al., 1996; Winslow et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Co-expression of BRAFV600E and PI3KαH1047R leads to development of lung tumors that show variable and widespread loss of expression of markers of AT2 pneumocyte terminal differentiation including the well-characterized surfactant proteins, SFTPA, SFTPB, and SFTPC.
source: By contrast, co-expression of BRAFV600E and PI3KαH1047R leads to development of lung tumors that show variable and widespread loss of expression of markers of AT2 pneumocyte terminal differentiation including the well-characterized surfactant proteins, SFTPA, SFTPB, and SFTPC.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on experimental observations.

claim: Reduced expression of AT2 markers begins early in tumor development and occurs despite sustained NKX2-1, FOXA1, and FOXA2 expression in tumor cells.
source: Notably reduced expression of AT2 markers begins early in tumor development and occurs despite sustained NKX2-1, FOXA1, and FOXA2 expression in tumor cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on experimental observations.

claim: Poorly differentiated and metastatic human lung adenocarcinomas often show loss of expression of functional markers of lung identity despite maintaining expression of NKX2-1.
source: Indeed, these findings bear similarity to observations in human lung adenocarcinomas in which poorly differentiated and metastatic cancers often show loss of expression of functional markers of lung identity despite maintaining expression of NKX2-1 (Yatabe et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: The BrafCAT allele functions analogously to the BrafCA allele for the development of benign lung tumors following CRE-mediated initiation of BRAFV600E expression.
source: Together, these data indicate that the BrafCAT allele functions analogously to the BrafCA allele for the development of benign lung tumors following CRE-mediated initiation of BRAFV600E expression, and that cells expressing the BRAFV600E-P2A-tdTomato mRNA are readily identified by flow cytometry within a short time frame.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on experimental observations comparing BrafCAT and BrafCA mice.

claim: Cells expressing the BRAFV600E-P2A-tdTomato mRNA are readily identified by flow cytometry within a short time frame.
source: Together, these data indicate that the BrafCAT allele functions analogously to the BrafCA allele for the development of benign lung tumors following CRE-mediated initiation of BRAFV600E expression, and that cells expressing the BRAFV600E-P2A-tdTomato mRNA are readily identified by flow cytometry within a short time frame.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on experimental observations.

claim: tdTomato fluorescence was detected by flow cytometry within 24 hr after expression of CRE in BrafCAT MEFs and plateaued by 96 hr.
source: In embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) derived from BrafCAT mice, tdTomato fluorescence was detected by flow cytometry within 24 hr after expression of CRE and plateaued by 96 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by a figure showing flow cytometry data.

claim: The total amount of fluorescence from the BrafCAT allele is modest, likely due to being driven by the endogenous Braf promoter.
source: Following CRE-mediated recombination of BrafCAT in both MEFs and mouse lung cells (Figure 2B), the total amount of fluorescence from the BrafCAT allele was modest, likely due to being driven by the endogenous Braf promoter.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on experimental observations.

claim: tdTomato expressing cells were readily differentiated from autofluorescence by using a channel with no fluorophore (FITC) as a marker of autofluorescence.
source: However, tdTomato expressing cells were readily differentiated from autofluorescence by using a channel with no fluorophore (FITC) as a marker of autofluorescence, as has been previously described (Dane et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by a citation.

claim: GSEA revealed that PI3K→AKT→MTOR signaling related genes were significantly elevated in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
source: Comparing 'hallmark' gene sets (Broad Institute MSigDB: Hallmarks), and consistent with the engineered characteristics of the lung tumor cells, GSEA revealed that PI3K→AKT→MTOR signaling (Figure 2C and D) and epithelial→mesenchymal transition (Figure 2C and E) related genes were significantly elevated in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in figures.

claim: Epithelial→mesenchymal transition related genes were significantly elevated in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
source: Comparing 'hallmark' gene sets (Broad Institute MSigDB: Hallmarks), and consistent with the engineered characteristics of the lung tumor cells, GSEA revealed that PI3K→AKT→MTOR signaling (Figure 2C and D) and epithelial→mesenchymal transition (Figure 2C and E) related genes were significantly elevated in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in figures.

claim: BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R expressing tumor cells showed a significant decrease (adj. p=0.01) in expression of transcripts associated with AT2 cell identity compared to BRAFV600E expressing tumor cells.
source: GSEA using these gene sets demonstrated that, compared to BRAFV600E expressing tumor cells, BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R expressing tumor cells showed a significant decrease (adj. p=0.01) in expression of transcripts associated with AT2 cell identity (Figure 2C and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in figures.

claim: The loss of expression of AT2 mRNAs was the strongest effect observed in association with PI3KαH1047R expression when examined in parallel with 50 hallmark gene sets and markers of other cell types in the distal lung epithelium.
source: Notably, when examined in parallel with 50 hallmark gene sets and markers of other cell types in the distal lung epithelium, the loss of expression of AT2 mRNAs was the strongest effect observed in association with PI3KαH1047R expression (NES: −2.71, Figure 2C and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in figures.

claim: Decreased AT2 marker expression was statistically significant as early as 2 weeks post-initiation.
source: Decreased AT2 marker expression was statistically significant as early as 2 weeks (Figure 3A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and was also observed at 6 weeks (Figure 3B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and 12 weeks (Figure 3C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) p.i.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by figures showing GSEA analysis at different time points.

claim: The effects of PI3KαH1047R on expression of AT2 differentiation markers initiates more rapidly than has been reported in tumors driven by KRASG12D, KRASG12D/TP53Null, KRASG12D/CTNNB1Δex3, BRAFV600E/TP53Null, or BRAFV600E/CTNNB1Δex3.
source: Hence the effects of PI3KαH1047R on expression of AT2 differentiation markers initiates more rapidly than has been reported in tumors driven by KRASG12D (Desai et al., 2014), KRASG12D/TP53Null (Winslow et al., 2011), KRASG12D/CTNNB1Δex3 (Pacheco-Pinedo et al., 2011), BRAFV600E/TP53Null (Garnett et al., 2017; Shai et al., 2015), or BRAFV600E/CTNNB1Δex3 (Juan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on comparison with cited studies.

claim: PI3KαH1047R expression elicited a marked increase in AT1 marker expression when comparing all time points.
source: In addition to reduced AT2 mRNA marker expression, PI3KαH1047R expression elicited a marked increase in AT1 marker expression when comparing all time points (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in a figure.

claim: The increase in AT1 marker expression was most significant at earlier time points and was no longer observed to be significant by 12 weeks post-initiation.
source: By contrast to the changes observed in AT2 marker expression, this change was most significant at earlier time points and was no longer observed to be significant by 12 weeks p.i. (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by a supplementary figure.

claim: Ad5-Sftpc-CRE initiated BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors displayed decreased expression of surfactant proteins A and C (SFTPA and SFTPC) and Lysozyme.
source: Consistent with the mRNA expression data, Ad5-Sftpc-CRE initiated BRAFV600E/ PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors displayed decreased expression of surfactant proteins A and C (SFTPA and SFTPC) and Lysozyme, all of which are AT2 pneumocyte markers (Figure 3B,D and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: Significant reductions of SFTPA, SFTPC, and LYZ expression were observed at 12 weeks post-initiation (Wilcoxon p=0.0001, .02, .02 respectively).
source: By this means we noted significant reductions of SFTPA, SFTPC, and LYZ expression at 12 weeks p.i. (Figure 3C, E and G. Wilcoxon p=0.0001,. 02,. 02 respectively, data from Figure 3—source data 1, 2 and 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images.

claim: Within each BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-induced tumor, variegated loss of AT2 marker expression was observed.
source: First, there did not appear to be two classes of BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-induced tumors with respect to AT2 marker expression. Instead, within each tumor we observed variegated loss of AT2 marker expression (Figure 3B,D,F insets).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: CCA staining was readily detectable in airways but was not observed throughout the BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors, including those cells that have reduced AT2 marker expression.
source: Second, to test whether CCA/SFTPC double positive cells might be the source of emergence of a separate tumor type, we co-stained our AT2 marker panel with antisera to detect expression of club cell antigen (CCA). While CCA staining was readily detectable in airways, it was not observed throughout the BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors, including those cells that have reduced AT2 marker expression (Figure 3B,D and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: Tumors arising in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven mice arose predominantly within alveolar spaces, a pattern characteristic of AT2-derived tumors.
source: Finally, we observed tumors arising predominantly within alveolar spaces, a pattern characteristic of AT2-derived tumors, whereas club cell derived tumors tend to arise predominantly at bronchioalveolar duct junctions (Cicchini et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on experimental observations and comparison with cited studies.

claim: BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors arise from AT2 cells but rapidly lose their differentiated identity under the influence of PI3'-lipid signaling.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven lung tumors arise from AT2 cells but rapidly lose their differentiated identity under the influence of PI3'-lipid signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: The NKX2-1 and FOXA1/2 transcription factors pattern and maintain the differentiated identity of normal lung cells.
source: Extensive research demonstrates that the NKX2-1 and FOXA1/2 transcription factors pattern and maintain the differentiated identity of normal lung cells (Bruno et al., 1995; Camolotto et al., 2018; DeFelice et al., 2003; Hamvas et al., 2013; Lazzaro et al., 1991; Minoo et al., 1995; Snyder et al., 2013; Stahlman et al., 1996; Yuan et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by citations.

claim: Analysis of RNA-Seq data showed no consistent decrease of NKX2-1 or FOXA1/2 mRNA expression in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven lung tumors.
source: Analysis of RNA-Seq data showed no consistent decrease of NKX2-1 or FOXA1/2 mRNA expression in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven lung tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: The observed loss of AT2 identity is not associated with a decrease or change in nuclear localization of NKX2-1 at either 2 or 12 weeks post-initiation.
source: Dual color immunofluorescence staining demonstrated that the observed loss of AT2 identity is not associated with a decrease or change in nuclear localization of NKX2-1 at either 2 or 12 weeks p.i. (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: There was no significant alteration in nuclear NKX2-1 staining at 2 weeks post-initiation.
source: Quantification of immunostaining supports this observation, with no significant alteration in nuclear NKX2-1 staining at 2 weeks, and only a slight but significant increase in nuclear NKX2-1 staining observed when comparing 12 week p.i. BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors to paired BRAFV600E-driven tumors (Figure 4C, data from Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images.

claim: A slight but significant increase in nuclear NKX2-1 staining was observed when comparing 12 week post-initiation BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors to paired BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
source: Quantification of immunostaining supports this observation, with no significant alteration in nuclear NKX2-1 staining at 2 weeks, and only a slight but significant increase in nuclear NKX2-1 staining observed when comparing 12 week p.i. BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors to paired BRAFV600E-driven tumors (Figure 4C, data from Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images.

claim: A significant decrease of SFTPA staining in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors was first observed at 2 weeks and persisted at 12 weeks post-initiation.
source: Quantification of the same tumors confirmed a significant decrease of SFTPA staining in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors first observed at 2 weeks and persisting at 12 weeks p.i. (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images.

claim: BRAFV600E-driven tumors show association of NKX2-1 and SFTPA staining consistent across time points (Spearman Rho = 0.23-.27).
source: BRAFV600E-driven tumors show association of NKX2-1 and SFTPA staining consistent across time points (Spearman Rho = 0.23-.27, Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors initially show almost no association between levels of NKX2-1 and SFTPA (Spearman Rho = 0.07).
source: BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors by contrast initially show almost no association between levels of NKX2-1 and SFTPA (Spearman Rho = 0.07, Figure 4F), but by 12 weeks p.i. the association of these two markers has increased markedly (Spearman Rho = 0.40, Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: By 12 weeks post-initiation, the association of NKX2-1 and SFTPA in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors has increased markedly (Spearman Rho = 0.40).
source: BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors by contrast initially show almost no association between levels of NKX2-1 and SFTPA (Spearman Rho = 0.07, Figure 4F), but by 12 weeks p.i. the association of these two markers has increased markedly (Spearman Rho = 0.40, Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: At both 2 and 12 weeks post-initiation, the largest proportional increase driven by PIK3CAH1047R expression is seen in NKX2-1+/SFTPA- tumor cells.
source: At both 2 and 12 weeks p.i., the largest proportional increase driven by PIK3CAH1047R expression is seen in NKX2-1+/SFTPA- tumor cells (Figure 4G–H), implying that at both early and late time points, decreased expression of NKX2-1 cannot explain the observed decrease in SFTPA expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by analysis shown in figures.

claim: Decreased expression of NKX2-1 cannot explain the observed decrease in SFTPA expression at both early and late time points.
source: At both 2 and 12 weeks p.i., the largest proportional increase driven by PIK3CAH1047R expression is seen in NKX2-1+/SFTPA- tumor cells (Figure 4G–H), implying that at both early and late time points, decreased expression of NKX2-1 cannot explain the observed decrease in SFTPA expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on inference from data analysis.

claim: Neither the expression of FOXA1 nor FOXA2 at 12 weeks post-initiation correlated with decreased SFTPA expression as assessed by immunostaining.
source: Similarly, neither the expression of FOXA1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) nor FOXA2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) at 12 weeks p.i. correlated with decreased SFTPA expression as assessed by immunostaining.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images in supplementary figures.

claim: The phosphorylation status of NKX2-1 at a critical ERK targeted residue (pS327) is not associated with loss of SFTPA expression.
source: Nor is the phosphorylation status of NKX2-1 at a critical ERK targeted residue (pS327) associated with loss of SFTPA expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images in a supplementary figure.

claim: The decreased expression of markers of AT2 cell differentiation observed upon co-activation of PI3'-lipid signaling in BRAFV600E driven tumors is largely independent of the expression levels of NKX2-1, FOXA1, and FOXA2.
source: Together these data suggest that the decreased expression of markers of AT2 cell differentiation that we observed upon co-activation of PI3'-lipid signaling in BRAFV600E driven tumors is largely independent of the expression levels of these known regulators of AT2 cell identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: A similar and significant decrease in SFTPA expression was observed comparing KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R- to KRASG12D-driven tumors at 16 weeks post-initiation.
source: Indeed, in this model, we observed a similar and significant decrease in SFTPA expression comparing KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R- to KRASG12D-driven tumors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E,G, data from Figure 4—source data 2), which did not correspond to reduced NKX2-1 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in supplementary figures.

claim: The decrease in SFTPA expression in KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors did not correspond to reduced NKX2-1 expression.
source: Indeed, in this model, we observed a similar and significant decrease in SFTPA expression comparing KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R- to KRASG12D-driven tumors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E,G, data from Figure 4—source data 2), which did not correspond to reduced NKX2-1 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in supplementary figures.

claim: Extensive loss of SFTPA immunoreactivity was not observed in KRASG12D-driven tumors.
source: Intriguingly, although mutationally-activated KRASG12D is reported to activate PI3'-lipid signaling in lung tumors (Castellano et al., 2013; Engelman et al., 2008; Gupta et al., 2007b; Molina-Arcas et al., 2013; Murillo et al., 2018; Rodriguez-Viciana et al., 1994), we did not observe extensive loss of SFTPA immunoreactivity in these tumors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images in a supplementary figure.

claim: Both KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors and KRASG12D-driven tumors showed similarly modest association of SFTPA and NKX2-1 expression.
source: Both KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors and KRASG12D-driven tumors showed similarly modest association of SFTPA and NKX2-1 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H–I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by correlation analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: There exist additional factors that regulate AT2 pneumocyte identity independently of the NKX2-1/FOXA1/FOXA2 regulatory axis, or these well-known regulators of pneumocyte identity require the presence of one or more additional factor(s) for their transcriptional function.
source: Taken together these data suggest that either there exist additional factors that regulate AT2 pneumocyte identity independently of the NKX2-1/FOXA1/FOXA2 regulatory axis, or that these well-known regulators of pneumocyte identity require the presence of one or more additional factor(s) for their transcriptional function.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: A striking increase in AQP5 expression was observed when comparing BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors to BRAFV600E-driven tumors at 2 weeks post-initiation.
source: At 2 weeks p.i. we observed a striking increase in AQP5 expression when comparing BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors to BRAFV600E-driven tumors (Figure 5A and B, data from Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification.

claim: At 12 weeks post-initiation, the difference in AQP5 immunoreactivity is no longer significant between BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R and BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
source: Interestingly, at 12 weeks p.i. the difference in AQP5 immunoreactivity is no longer significant between BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R and BRAFV600E-driven tumors, mirroring our mRNA expression profiling results (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification.

claim: BRAFV600E-driven tumors display widespread expression of both AT1 marker AQP5 and AT2 marker LYZ.
source: Co-immunostaining of AQP5 and LYZ showed similar patterns in which BRAFV600E-driven tumors display widespread expression of both of AT1 and AT2 markers (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors show some areas that are double positive for both AQP5 and LYZ, some areas with only expression of AQP5, some areas with only expression of LYZ, and some areas where neither is expressed.
source: By contrast, BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors show some areas that are double positive for both AQP5 and LYZ (Figure 5C, cyan arrowheads), some areas with only expression of AQP5 (Figure 5C, green arrowheads), some areas with only expression of LYZ (Figure 5C, red arrowheads), and some areas where neither is expressed (Figure 5C, yellow arrowheads).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: BRAFV600E-driven tumors show correlation (Spearman Rho = 0.54) between AQP5 and LYZ.
source: Quantification of these data shows correlation (Spearman Rho = 0.54) between AQP5 and LYZ in BRAFV600E-driven tumors (Figure 5D), but lower correlation (Spearman Rho = 0.13) between these markers in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors show lower correlation (Spearman Rho = 0.13) between AQP5 and LYZ.
source: Quantification of these data shows correlation (Spearman Rho = 0.54) between AQP5 and LYZ in BRAFV600E-driven tumors (Figure 5D), but lower correlation (Spearman Rho = 0.13) between these markers in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by correlation analysis shown in a figure.

claim: BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors show a strong decrease in AQP5+/LYZ+ double positive cells, with corresponding increases in each of the remaining classes of cells (AQP5+/LYZ-; AQP5-/LYZ+; and AQP5-/LYZ-).
source: Comparing these two tumor types directly shows a significant effect of genotype on staining distribution (Figure 5F), with BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors showing a strong decrease in AQP5+/LYZ+ double positive cells, with corresponding increases in each of the remaining classes of cells (AQP5+/LYZ-; AQP5-/LYZ+; and AQP5-/LYZ-).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Normal AT2 cells display a cuboidal morphology and contain many surfactant rich lamellar bodies.
source: Normal AT2 cells display a cuboidal morphology and contain many surfactant rich lamellar bodies (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, cyan).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by an electron micrograph in a supplementary figure.

claim: BRAFV600E-driven tumor cells displayed gross morphological similarities to AT2 cells.
source: BRAFV600E-driven tumor cells displayed gross morphological similarities to AT2 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), but in a subset of tumor cells large vacuoles, not seen in normal AT2 cells, were observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, purple).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by an electron micrograph in a supplementary figure.

claim: In a subset of BRAFV600E-driven tumor cells, large vacuoles not seen in normal AT2 cells were observed.
source: BRAFV600E-driven tumor cells displayed gross morphological similarities to AT2 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), but in a subset of tumor cells large vacuoles, not seen in normal AT2 cells, were observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, purple).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by an electron micrograph in a supplementary figure.

claim: Enhanced magnification of vacuoles in BRAFV600E-driven tumor cells demonstrated a rough chrysanthemum like pattern of electron dense material characteristic of glycogen storage.
source: Enhanced magnification of these structures demonstrated a rough chrysanthemum like pattern of electron dense material (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) characteristic of glycogen storage (Revel, 1960).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by an electron micrograph in a supplementary figure and a citation.

claim: Glycogen storage vacuoles are a hallmark of bipotent progenitor cells.
source: As glycogen storage vacuoles are another hallmark of bipotent progenitor cells (Desai et al., 2014), we propose that BRAFV600E→MEK→ERK signaling alone drives AT2 pneumocytes toward this fate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by a citation.

claim: BRAFV600E→MEK→ERK signaling alone drives AT2 pneumocytes toward a bipotent progenitor cell fate.
source: As glycogen storage vacuoles are another hallmark of bipotent progenitor cells (Desai et al., 2014), we propose that BRAFV600E→MEK→ERK signaling alone drives AT2 pneumocytes toward this fate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on inference from experimental observations and cited literature.

claim: The coincident activation of ERK1/2 plus PI3'-lipid signaling promotes more profound de-differentiation of AT2 cells.
source: As BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors show some cells with co-expression of AT1 and AT2 markers, and many cells with reductions of either or both of these marker classes, we believe the coincident activation of ERK1/2 plus PI3'-lipid signaling promotes more profound de-differentiation of AT2 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: The majority of the AT2-100 and AT1-100 mRNAs fell into a single cluster (Cluster 2 – Dark blue) in WGCNA analysis.
source: The majority of the AT2-100 and AT1-100 mRNAs fell into a single cluster (Cluster 2 – Dark blue Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by WGCNA analysis shown in figures.

claim: PGC1α is a nuclear receptor co-activator that clusters with the majority of AT1 and AT2 genes and its mRNA is significantly decreased in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors.
source: The intersection of these three methods left a single candidate, the nuclear receptor co-activator, PGC1α (Figure 6D). PGC1α is a known transcriptional regulator, clusters with the majority of AT1 and AT2 genes, and its mRNA is significantly decreased in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by WGCNA analysis and differential expression analysis shown in figures.

claim: Human lung tumors bearing mutations in either PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN have significantly reduced PPARGC1A mRNA expression compared to tumors bearing none of these mutations.
source: The control of PPARGC1A levels by PI3'-lipid signaling may also be true in human lung tumors: those bearing mutations in either PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN have significantly reduced PPARGC1A mRNA expression compared to tumors bearing none of these mutations (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by analysis of human lung adenocarcinoma data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Cells with decreased expression of SFTPA lack nuclear PGC1α in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors.
source: Immunostaining revealed that cells with decreased expression of SFTPA lack nuclear PGC1α (Figure 6F, red arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: Tumor cells with detectable nuclear localization of PGC1α display readily detectable levels of SFTPA in BRAFV600E/PI3KαH1047R-driven tumors.
source: Conversely, tumor cells with detectable nuclear localization of PGC1α display readily detectable levels of SFTPA (Figure 6F, green arrows).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images.

claim: BRAFV600E/PGC1αNull-driven lung tumor cells showed decreased expression of mRNAs encoding proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation.
source: As expected, BRAFV600E/PGC1αNull-driven lung tumor cells showed decreasd expression of mRNAs encoding proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in a figure.

claim: BRAFV600E/PGC1αNull-driven tumors displayed a widespread decrease in markers of AT2 differentiation status as compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors that retain PGC1α expression.
source: BRAFV600E/PGC1αNull-driven tumors also displayed a widespread decrease in markers of AT2 differentiation status as compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors that retain PGC1α expression (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in figures.

claim: Silencing of PGC1α recapitulated some aspects of PI3Kα activation, including increasing markers of EMT.
source: Interestingly, silencing of PGC1α recapitulated some other aspects of PI3Kα activation, including increasing markers of EMT, but some noticeable differences were observed in mRNA profiles including significant increases in ciliated and club cell markers (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Silencing of PGC1α resulted in significant increases in ciliated and club cell markers.
source: Interestingly, silencing of PGC1α recapitulated some other aspects of PI3Kα activation, including increasing markers of EMT, but some noticeable differences were observed in mRNA profiles including significant increases in ciliated and club cell markers (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by GSEA analysis shown in a figure.

claim: LYZ and SFTPA immunoreactivity in BRAFV600E and BRAFV600E/PGC1αNull-driven tumors validated the decrease in AT2 marker expression in the absence of PGC1α expression.
source: LYZ and SFTPA immunoreactivity in BRAFV600E and BRAFV600E/PGC1αNull-driven tumors validated the decrease in AT2 marker expression in the absence of PGC1α expression (Figure 7B–C, data from Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification.

claim: The most enriched novel motif in the promoter regions of AT2-100 genes bears significant similarity to the known binding motif of the nuclear receptor, NR5A2.
source: The most enriched novel motif (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–C) bears significant similarity to the known binding motif of the nuclear receptor, NR5A2 (JASPAR: MA0505.1), also known as Liver Receptor Homolog (LRH) 1 (Gupta et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by motif discovery analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Transfection of individual expression constructs for NR5A2, PGC1α, NKX2-1, or FOXA1 showed modest promoter induction of up to four fold over mock-transfected cells.
source: Transfection of individual expression constructs for NR5A2, PGC1α, NKX2-1, or FOXA1 showed modest promoter induction of up to four fold over mock-transfected cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by luciferase assay data shown in a figure.

claim: Co-transfection of NR5A2, PGC1α, NKX2-1, and FOXA1 together showed a dramatic 25–100 fold induction of the SFTPA, SFTPB, and SFTPC promoters.
source: However, co-transfection of these four factors together showed a dramatic 25–100 fold induction of the SFTPA, SFTPB, and SFTPC promoters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on luciferase assay data.

claim: The absence of PGC1α severely hampered the ability of NKX2-1 and FOXA1 to transactivate the surfactant A and B promoters.
source: Importantly, the absence of PGC1α severely hampered the ability of NKX2-1 and FOXA1 to transactivate the surfactant A and B promoters, suggesting a functional role of PGC1α in the transcriptional transactivation of AT2 promoters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on luciferase assay data.

claim: Magnetic beads conjugated to a mouse monoclonal antibody directed against PGC1α readily co-immunoprecipitated NKX2-1 from MLE-12 cell extracts.
source: While magnetic beads conjugated to mouse IgG did not enrich eluates for NKX2-1, magnetic beads conjugated to a mouse monoclonal antibody directed against PGC1α readily co-immunoprecipitated NKX2-1 (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in a figure.

claim: Magnetic beads conjugated to a rabbit monoclonal antibody directed against NKX2-1 co-immunoprecipitated PGC1α from MLE-12 cell extracts.
source: To confirm this result, we showed that, while magnetic beads conjugated to rabbit IgG did not enrich eluates for PGC1α, magnetic beads conjugated to a rabbit monoclonal antibody directed against NKX2-1 also co-immunoprecipitated PGC1α (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in a figure.

claim: PGC1α and NKX2-1 appear to co-exist in a complex in cells that express genes encoding AT2 expressed surfactant proteins.
source: Thus, PGC1α and NKX2-1 appear to co-exist in a complex in cells that express genes encoding AT2 expressed surfactant proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: BRAFV600E-driven lung cancer kills ~4000 patients per year in the U.S.A.
source: Here we describe a new GEM model that has allowed a deeper dissection of the stages of BRAFV600E-driven lung cancer, a disease that kills ~4000 patients per year in the U.S.A. (Siegel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: All BRAFV600E expressing cells are predicted to be red fluorescent by virtue of co-expression of tdTomato in the BrafCAT mouse.
source: Consequently, all BRAFV600E expressing cells are predicted to be red fluorescent by virtue of co-expression of tdTomato.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on the design of the BrafCAT allele.

claim: The main disadvantage of the BrafCAT approach is the modest fluorescence emission of tdTomato when expressed downstream of a P2A element from the mutationally activated BrafT1910A mRNA.
source: The main disadvantage of our approach appears to be the modest fluorescence emission of tdTomato when expressed downstream of a P2A element from the mutationally activated BrafT1910A mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on experimental observations.

claim: The level of tdTomato fluorescence in lung tumors arising in BrafCAT mice is readily detected by flow cytometry.
source: Hence, although the level of tdTomato fluorescence in lung tumors arising in BrafCAT mice is readily detected by flow cytometry, detection of tdTomato expression by immunohistochemistry in FFPE tissue sections is problematic.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on experimental observations.

claim: Detection of tdTomato expression by immunohistochemistry in FFPE tissue sections is problematic in BrafCAT mice.
source: Hence, although the level of tdTomato fluorescence in lung tumors arising in BrafCAT mice is readily detected by flow cytometry, detection of tdTomato expression by immunohistochemistry in FFPE tissue sections is problematic.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on experimental observations.

claim: The use of a fluorophore expressed in trans approach inherently relies on the simultaneous activity of CRE at distinct regions of the genome.
source: By contrast, the use of a fluorophore expressed in trans approach inherently relies on the simultaneous activity of CRE at distinct regions of the genome.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on knowledge of how CRE-lox systems work.

claim: It is possible for the proto-oncogenic BrafCA locus to be subject to CRE-mediated recombination without recombination of the reporter, or vice-versa, when using a fluorophore expressed in trans approach.
source: Thus it is possible for the proto-oncogenic BrafCA locus to be subject to CRE-mediated recombination without recombination of the reporter, or vice-versa.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on knowledge of how CRE-lox systems work.

claim: The BrafCAT approach avoids the noise inherent in fluorophore expressed in trans approaches and results in a level of fluorescence that is directly correlated with expression of BRAFV600E on a cell-by-cell basis.
source: Our approach avoids this noise entirely and results in a level of fluorescence that is directly correlated with expression of BRAFV600E on a cell-by-cell basis (van Veen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: The BrafCAT approach is especially compatible with the emerging technology of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq).
source: Importantly, our approach is especially compatible with the emerging technology of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq), in which it is desirable to isolate single BRAFV600E oncoprotein kinase expressing cells for analysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on inference about the utility of the BrafCAT approach.

claim: Nearly every AT2 identity marker is diminished in expression in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors as compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors, as early as two weeks post-initiation.
source: Analysis of the full complement of AT2 markers paints a dramatic picture; nearly every AT2 identity marker is diminished in expression in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors as compared to BRAFV600E-driven tumors, as early as two weeks p.i.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on GSEA analysis.

claim: A similar early and consistent repression of PGC1α expression was noted in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors.
source: Importantly we noted a similar early and consistent repression of PGC1α expression in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on RNA-Seq data.

claim: PGC1α expression is repressed by the PI3K→AKT signaling axis via three insulin response sequences found in the PGC1α promoter shown to bind to the AKT-regulated FOXO1 transcription factor.
source: Here our data support previous findings that indicate that PGC1α expression is repressed by the PI3K→AKT signaling axis via three insulin response sequences found in the PGC1α promoter shown to bind to the AKT-regulated FOXO1 transcription factor (Daitoku et al., 2003; Kemper et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by citations.

claim: BRAFV600E signaling can suppress PGC1α expression via the MITF transcription factor in melanoma.
source: It has also been suggested that BRAFV600E signaling can suppress PGC1α expression via the MITF transcription factor in melanoma, further demonstrating the complicated interplay between growth factor signaling and oxidative phosphorylation (Haq et al., 2013), though this study did not examine any potential connection of PGC1α to tumor cell differentiation status.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: PIK3CA mutation is found in ~4% of human LUAD.
source: PIK3CA mutation is found in ~4% of human LUAD (Campbell et al., 2016) that, although quite rare, still represents a significant patient population due to the high prevalence of lung cancer in our society.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: The ability of mutationally-activated KRASG12D to bind and activate PI3Kα is critical for its tumor promoting activities, as well as tumor maintenance.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that the ability of mutationally-activated KRASG12D to bind and activate PI3Kα is critical for its tumor promoting activities, as well as tumor maintenance (Castellano et al., 2013; Gupta et al., 2007b; Molina-Arcas et al., 2013; Murillo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by citations.

claim: Activation of PI3'-lipid signaling remains rate limiting with respect to tumor initiation and growth in KRASG12D-driven lung tumors as evidenced by the strong cooperation between KRASG12D and PIK3CAH1047R in promoting lung tumorigenesis in a GEM model.
source: Despite this, activation of PI3'-lipid signaling remains rate limiting with respect to tumor initiation and growth in KRASG12D-driven lung tumors as evidenced by the strong cooperation between KRASG12D and PIK3CAH1047R in promoting lung tumorigenesis in a GEM model (Green et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: The initial expression of KRASG12D is a relatively weak activator of both PI3'-lipid signaling and the RAF→MEK→ERK pathways.
source: This cooperation likely reflects the fact that the initial expression of KRASG12D is a relatively weak activator of both PI3'-lipid signaling and the RAF→MEK→ERK pathways (Cicchini et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: KRASG12D derived lung cancer cells show little phosphorylation of AKT at a key activating amino acid (S473).
source: Indeed, whereas KRASG12D derived lung cancer cells show little phosphorylation of AKT at a key activating amino acid (S473), KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R derived cells show strong pS473-AKT phosphorylation (Green et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R derived cells show strong pS473-AKT phosphorylation.
source: Indeed, whereas KRASG12D derived lung cancer cells show little phosphorylation of AKT at a key activating amino acid (S473), KRASG12D/PIK3CAH1047R derived cells show strong pS473-AKT phosphorylation (Green et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: The lack of PI3'-lipid signaling in KRASG12D-driven lung tumors is not only limiting in tumor growth, but in propensity for AT2 pneumocyte de-differentiation.
source: Our results suggest that the lack of PI3'-lipid signaling in KRASG12D-driven lung tumors is not only limiting in tumor growth, but in propensity for AT2 pneumocyte de-differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: Stromally derived IGF-1 promotes a cancer stem cell like phenotype in Kras mutated cell lines via the PI3K→AKT signaling axis.
source: Intriguingly, recent studies have shown that stromally derived IGF-1 promotes a cancer stem cell like phenotype in Kras mutated cell lines (Chen et al., 2014), via the PI3K→AKT signaling axis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: Lung adenocarcinoma differentiation status, as judged by pathological criteria, remains a critically important prognostic factor in predicting patient survival.
source: Lung adenocarcinoma differentiation status, as judged by pathological criteria, remains a critically important prognostic factor in predicting patient survival (Yoshizawa et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: In the KrasLSL-G12D GEM model of KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma, NKX2-1 expression is diminished or silenced in the most poorly differentiated tumors.
source: Indeed, in the KrasLSL-G12D GEM model of KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma, NKX2-1 expression is diminished or silenced in the most poorly differentiated tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on cited literature.

claim: shRNA-mediated inhibition of NKX2-1 expression is reported to enhance the metastatic potential of KRASG12D/TP53Null-driven lung cancer cells.
source: Moreover, shRNA-mediated inhibition of NKX2-1 expression is reported to enhance the metastatic potential of KRASG12D/TP53Null-driven lung cancer cells (Winslow et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: Concomitant expression of KRASG12D with genetic silencing of NKX2-1 expression promotes trans-differentiation of tumor cells into a gastric fate resembling de-differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma.
source: Interestingly, concomitant expression of KRASG12D with genetic silencing of NKX2-1 expression has qualitatively different effects, promoting trans-differentiation of tumor cells into a gastric fate resembling de-differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma (Snyder et al., 2013), an effect that requires the activity of FOXA1/FOXA2 (Camolotto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by citations.

claim: Trans-differentiation of tumor cells into a gastric fate resembling de-differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma requires the activity of FOXA1/FOXA2.
source: Interestingly, concomitant expression of KRASG12D with genetic silencing of NKX2-1 expression has qualitatively different effects, promoting trans-differentiation of tumor cells into a gastric fate resembling de-differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma (Snyder et al., 2013), an effect that requires the activity of FOXA1/FOXA2 (Camolotto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by citations.

claim: Haploinsufficiency of NKX2-1 promoted the appearance of mucinous adenocarcinoma in the KrasLSL-G12D GEM model of lung adenocarcinoma.
source: Intriguingly, while even haploinsufficiency of NKX2-1 promoted the appearance of mucinous adenocarcinoma in the KrasLSL-G12D GEM model of lung adenocarcinoma, the same was not true in a lung adenocarcinoma model driven by expression of a mutationally-activated form of the EGF receptor (Maeda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: Haploinsufficiency of NKX2-1 slowed tumor progression in a lung adenocarcinoma model driven by expression of a mutationally-activated form of the EGF receptor.
source: In this model, haploinsufficiency of NKX2-1 slowed tumor progression rather than enhancing it.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on cited literature.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations or silencing of NKX2-1 is a relatively infrequent event in lung adenocarcinoma.
source: Importantly, loss-of-function mutations or silencing of NKX2-1 is a relatively infrequent event in lung adenocarcinoma.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on knowledge of lung adenocarcinoma genetics.

claim: NKX2-1 is often found as the most significantly focally amplified locus in lung adenocarcinoma.
source: Instead NKX2-1 is often found as the most significantly focally amplified locus (Campbell et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: In human NSCLC cell lines in which NKX2-1 is amplified, RNAi-mediated inhibition of NKX2-1 expression elicited decreased cell division and apoptosis.
source: Further, in human NSCLC cell lines in which NKX2-1 is amplified, RNAi-mediated inhibition of NKX2-1 expression elicited decreased cell division and apoptosis (Kwei et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: The role of NKX2-1 in LUAD progression is simultaneously critically important and also complicated.
source: Hence, the role of NKX2-1 in LUAD progression is thus simultaneously critically important and also complicated.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on inference from cited literature.

claim: GEM models provide an ideal system in which to study the contribution of individual mutations to each step of tumor initiation and progression without the complications of mutagen-induced genome hypermutation as is common in KRAS-mutated human lung cancer cells.
source: In this case, GEM models provide an ideal system in which to study the contribution of individual mutations to each step of tumor initiation and progression without the complications of mutagen-induced genome hypermutation as is common in KRAS-mutated human lung cancer cells (Chalmers et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.

claim: Transcriptional co-activators are critical for NKX2-1 function.
source: While a wealth of literature has shown the direct effect of NKX2-1 on AT2 promoters (Bruno et al., 1995), and the importance of NKX2-1 in normal lung development (DeFelice et al., 2003), it has also been shown that transcriptional co-activators are critical for NKX2-1 function (Cassel et al., 2002; Di Palma et al., 2003; Park et al., 2004; Yi et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by citations.

claim: The binding motif of the nuclear receptor, NR5A2 is highly enriched in the promoters of AT2 specific genes.
source: Here we have shown that the binding motif of the nuclear receptor, NR5A2 is highly enriched in the promoters of AT2 specific genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on motif discovery analysis.

claim: NR5A2 and its known co-factor PGC1α can potently enhance the activity of NKX2-1 at the promoters for surfactant proteins A and B.
source: We also demonstrate that NR5A2, and its known co-factor PGC1α (Yazawa et al., 2010), can potently enhance the activity of NKX2-1 at the promoters for surfactant proteins A and B.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on luciferase assay data and a citation.

claim: While NR5A2 and PGC1α can activate the promoter of SFTPC alone, the added presence of NKX2-1 and FOXA1 does not further co-activate this promoter.
source: Interestingly, while NR5A2 and PGC1α can activate the promoter of SFTPC alone, the added presence of NKX2-1 and FOXA1 does not further co-activate this promoter.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on luciferase assay data.

claim: In BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors, an early decrease of PGC1α mRNA expression was observed.
source: In vivo, in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors, we observed an early decrease of PGC1α mRNA expression, and importantly, a correlation between decreased PGC1α and SFTPA on a cell-by-cell basis within tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on RNA-Seq data.

claim: A correlation between decreased PGC1α and SFTPA on a cell-by-cell basis within tumors was observed in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors.
source: In vivo, in BRAFV600E/PIK3CAH1047R-driven tumors, we observed an early decrease of PGC1α mRNA expression, and importantly, a correlation between decreased PGC1α and SFTPA on a cell-by-cell basis within tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on immunofluorescence data.

claim: Mutational-activation of PI3'-lipid signaling in BRAFV600E-driven LUAD leads to diminished PGC1α expression, and this reduced expression compromises the ability of NKX2-1/FOXA1 to maintain AT2 pneumocyte identity.
source: Combined with functional data in GEM models in which PGC1α expression was genetically silenced, these data argue that mutational-activation of PI3'-lipid signaling in BRAFV600E-driven LUAD leads to diminished PGC1α expression, and that this reduced expression compromises the ability of NKX2-1/FOXA1 to maintain AT2 pneumocyte identity (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: While genetic silencing of PGC1α recapitulated some aspects of PI3K activation in BRAFV600E-driven driven lung tumors, there were interesting differences, including an increase in markers of club and ciliated cell identity, and no significant effect on AT1 marker expression.
source: It is important to note that while genetic silencing of PGC1α recapitulated some aspects of PI3K activation in BRAFV600E-driven driven lung tumors, there were interesting differences, including an increase in markers of club and ciliated cell identity, and no significant effect on AT1 marker expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on GSEA analysis.

claim: Amongst the pleiotropic effects of PI3'-lipid signaling, inhibition of PGC1α-mediated signaling represents one of many important effector pathways.
source: It is therefore highly likely that amongst the pleiotropic effects of PI3'-lipid signaling, inhibition of PGC1α-mediated signaling represents one of many important effector pathways.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on inference from experimental observations.

claim: This novel mechanism of lung identity regulation can be induced by mutational-activation of PI3Kα in both KRASG12D- and BRAFV600E-driven driven lung adenocarcinomas.
source: This novel mechanism of lung identity regulation is made more important by the observation that it can be induced by mutational-activation of PI3Kα in both KRASG12D- and BRAFV600E-driven driven lung adenocarcinomas.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on experimental observations in both mouse models.

claim: The best characterized role of PGC1α is in the regulation of mitochondrial biogenesis.
source: Since the best characterized role of PGC1α is in the regulation of mitochondrial biogenesis, we were initially surprised to discover the cooperativity that PGC1α shows in the regulation of AT2 cell identity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is based on knowledge of PGC1α function.

claim: Crippling mitochondrial function via loss of the critical pyruvate transporter, MPC1, potently drives cells into a de-differentiated stem cell fate in drosophila and mouse intestinal cells.
source: However, it has recently emerged that crippling mitochondrial function via loss of the critical pyruvate transporter, MPC1, potently drives cells into a de-differentiated stem cell fate in drosophila and mouse intestinal cells (Schell et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and is supported by a citation.
